summary: Iteration 4 — Website Development service + Sales RBAC team logins. Both backend and frontend verified end-to-end on the public preview URL. Backend: 23/23 regression + 16/16 new RBAC/Team tests passing (39/39). Frontend: all requested flows pass — home 4-col grid with 7 service tiles + 8th CTA tile (home-service-card-not-sure), home-service-card-website-development present, /services and footer list Website Development, /services/website-development loads with its own H1, /contact?service=Website preselects lead-form-type-website on step 2, admin Team panel can create/duplicate-error/toggle-active/reset-password/delete sales users, sales user login shows role badge 'SALES · <name>', only Leads tab visible, mobile tabbar hidden for sales. No horizontal overflow at 1920 or 390.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py: PERMS clean mapping; require() dependency is idiomatic. Good.

server.py sales_user() filters role==sales so admin cannot modify/delete admin via /users/{id} (returns 404). Correct for safety; however this also prevents an admin from managing other future admin accounts — acceptable for current single-admin model.

server.py update_user uses find_one_and_update without return_document=ReturnDocument.AFTER; motor defaults to BEFORE. Verify: it works in tests because fixtures re-fetch, but the API returns stale data to the Team UI (shows pre-update active/name until manual refresh). TeamPanel.jsx compensates by setting the local list from the response — users may see the switch flicker back momentarily. Minor UX issue; main agent may want to pass return_document=ReturnDocument.AFTER. Note: the e2e UI test still showed Disabled badge appearing correctly, likely because frontend sends the new state optimistically via the response body; worth double-checking.
server.py login endpoint computes locked_until via a two-step update (first $inc then conditional set) which could race under concurrent attempts; acceptable for small scale.
TeamPanel.jsx exposes new sales user password as plain text input (type='text') — intentional for admin visibility but ensure Team page is only reachable by admins (it is, via role gate).
